name: B.A. (Hons.) in Mass Communication (BMC)
description: Three-Year Undergraduate Degree Programme in Mass Communication (Bachelor of Mass Communication / B.A. Hons. in Mass Communication) under Choice Based Credit System (CBCS), Patna University. Offered at Patna College and the Centre for Mass Communication, this program prepares students for leadership in print journalism, television broadcasting, digital news, radio production, advertising, public relations, and visual communication.

papers.name: Introduction to Mass Communication
recommendedBooks: Mass Communication in India - Keval J. Kumar, Jaico Publishing
McQuail’s Mass Communication Theory - Denis McQuail, SAGE
Understanding Media - Marshall McLuhan, Routledge

units.title: Foundations & Process of Communication
topics: Concept, definition, nature and scope of communication; Human communication evolution from oral to digital era
Elements and process of communication: Sender, encoding, message, channel, receiver, decoding, feedback and noise
Levels of communication: Intrapersonal, interpersonal, group, public and mass communication
7 Cs of effective communication and communication barriers

units.title: Classic Models of Communication
topics: Linear models: Aristotle model, Harold Lasswell formula (Who says What in Which Channel to Whom with What Effect)
Claude Shannon and Warren Weaver Mathematical Model of Communication
Interactive and circular models: Wilbur Schramm, David Berlo (SMCR) Model, Newcomb ABX Model
Helical model of Frank Dance and Westley-MacLean conceptual model

units.title: Functions & Role of Mass Media
topics: Mass communication: Definition, distinct characteristics and audiences
Functions of mass media: Surveillance, correlation, cultural transmission, entertainment and economic mobilization
Dysfunctions of mass media: Narcotizing dysfunction, stereotyping and information overload

units.title: Mass Media & Society
topics: Relationship between mass media, democracy and civil society; Media as the Fourth Estate
Mass culture, popular culture, high culture and sub-cultures; Commercialization of media
Globalization of media and cultural imperialism debates

papers.name: History of Print Media & Indian Press
recommendedBooks: History of Indian Journalism - J. Natarajan, Publications Division
Press in India - G.N.S. Raghavan, Gyan Publishing House
Indian Journalism - Nadig Krishnamurthy, Prasaranga

units.title: Early Printing & Birth of Indian Press
topics: Invention of movable type printing press by Johannes Gutenberg and its socio-political impact
Introduction of printing technology in India by Christian missionaries
James Augustus Hicky and the Bengal Gazette (1780): Origins of newspaper journalism in India

units.title: Press in India’s Freedom Struggle
topics: Role of social reformers: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Mirat-ul-Akhbar, Sambad Kaumudi)
1857 revolt and the Gagging Act; Vernacular Press Act 1878 and struggle for press freedom
Nationalist press leaders: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Kesari, Mahratta), Mahatma Gandhi as journalist (Young India, Harijan, Indian Opinion)
Pioneering regional and national dailies: The Hindu, Amrita Bazar Patrika, The Statesman, The Indian Express

units.title: History of Hindi & Bihar Press
topics: First Hindi newspaper: Udant Martand (1826) published by Pt. Jugal Kishore Shukla
Growth of Hindi journalism: Bharatendu Harishchandra, Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi (Saraswati)
Evolution of press in Bihar: The Searchlight, The Indian Nation, Aryavarta, Pradeep and modern contemporary Hindi dailies

units.title: Post-Independence Press & Institutional Framework
topics: Press after independence: Challenges of nation building and development coverage
First Press Commission (1952-54) and Second Press Commission (1978-82) recommendations
Establishment and role of Press Council of India (PCI) and Registrar of Newspapers for India (RNI)

papers.name: Media Language & Creative Writing
recommendedBooks: Writing for the Media - Sunny Thomas, Oxford
The Elements of Style - William Strunk Jr. & E.B. White

units.title: Journalistic Language Principles
topics: Grammar, syntax, vocabulary, clarity, conciseness and punch in journalistic writing
Differences in writing style for print, radio, television and web media

units.title: Creative Non-Fiction & Feature Writing
topics: Feature stories: Types (human interest, profile, trend, travel, lifestyle)
Middle pieces, opinion editorials (Op-Ed), columns, letters to editor and creative narrative techniques

papers.name: Language Proficiency (English / Hindi)
recommendedBooks: High School English Grammar and Composition - Wren & Martin
Vyavaharik Hindi Vyakaran - Hardev Bahri

units.title: Functional Linguistic Competency
topics: Sentence structure, common errors, idioms, phrases and vocabulary enrichment
Reading comprehension, critical analysis and summarization of complex texts

units.title: Professional Expression
topics: Drafting official correspondence, circulars, press releases and executive summaries
Public speaking, pronunciation, oral presentation and participation in panel discussions

papers.name: Print Journalism & Reporting
recommendedBooks: Basic News Writing - Melvin Mencher, McGraw Hill
News Reporting and Writing - Brian S. Brooks et al., Bedford/St. Martin’s
The Journalist’s Handbook - M.V. Kamath, Vikas Publishing

units.title: Understanding News & News Values
topics: Definition, concept and elements of news: Timeliness, proximity, prominence, conflict, human interest, oddity and consequence
Types of news: Hard news vs soft news, breaking news, follow-up stories and backgrounders
News sources: Attribution, credibility, cultivating reliable confidential sources and press conferences

units.title: News Writing & Structure
topics: The 5 Ws and 1 H of news reporting; Inverted pyramid structure vs narrative storytelling
Anatomy of a news story: Headline, dateline, byline, lead/intro types (summary, quote, question, descriptive, punch), body and kicker/conclusion
Quotes, paraphrasing, balance, objectivity and fairness in reporting

units.title: Beat Reporting Specializations
topics: Beat system: Functions and duties of beat reporters
Reporting major beats: Political reporting, crime and court reporting, civic issues, sports journalism, business and economy, education and health
Investigative journalism: Techniques, sting operations, ethical challenges and investigative reporting cases

units.title: Interviewing Techniques & Fieldwork
topics: Types of interviews: Face-to-face, telephonic, press conferences, vox populi and investigative interviews
Preparation, formulating open-ended questions, handling hostile interviewees and taking notes
Practical news gathering assignments and filing news reports from Patna University campus and Patna city

papers.name: Editing & Newspaper Layout Design
recommendedBooks: The Art of Editing - Baskette, Sissors & Brooks, Allyn & Bacon
Modern Newspaper Editing - Gene Gilmore, Iowa State University Press
Newspaper Design - Harold Evans, Heinemann

units.title: News Desk & Editing Principles
topics: Structure and hierarchy of a newspaper newsroom: Editor-in-Chief, Resident Editor, News Editor, Chief Sub-Editor and Sub-Editors
Meaning and purpose of editing: Checking facts, ensuring balance, eliminating libellous material, pruning verbosity
Standard copy-editing symbols and stylebook adherence

units.title: Headline Writing & Captioning
topics: Significance and functions of headlines; Types of headlines: Banner, streamer, kicker, hammer, deck, label, question
Writing captivating and accurate headlines under space constraints
Photo captioning: 5 Ws in captions, cutlines, photo selection and photo cropping principles

units.title: Newspaper Layout & Design Principles
topics: Typography: Typefaces (serif vs sans-serif), font sizes, kerning, leading, column width
Principles of design: Balance, contrast, rhythm, unity, proportion and eye-movement flow on front page
Elements of page makeup: Masthead, folio, dateline, teasers, anchor stories, white space and infographic usage

units.title: Digital Desktop Publishing (DTP) Hands-on
topics: Introduction to DTP software: Adobe InDesign and QuarkXPress workspace and tools
Setting up multi-column newspaper grid templates and dummy sheets
Designing a laboratory newspaper / campus tabloid including dummy creation, text flow, headline placing and final PDF export

papers.name: Media Laws & Indian Constitution
recommendedBooks: Law of the Press in India - D.D. Basu, Prentice Hall of India
Media Law and Ethics - Neelamalar M., PHI Learning

units.title: Constitutional Guarantees & Press Freedom
topics: Freedom of Speech and Expression: Article 19(1)(a) of Indian Constitution; Reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2)
Key Supreme Court judgements on press freedom (Romesh Thappar, Sakal Papers, Bennett Coleman)
Parliamentary Privileges: Articles 105 and 194; Contempt of Legislature

units.title: Statutory Media Acts & Information Law
topics: Defamation: Civil and criminal defamation under IPC Sections 499 & 500, legal defenses
Contempt of Courts Act 1971: Civil vs criminal contempt; Official Secrets Act 1923
Right to Information (RTI) Act 2005: Filing applications, appellate authorities, exemptions under Section 8
Working Journalists Act, Press and Registration of Books Act, Copyright Act and Fair Use doctrine

papers.name: Environmental Sustainability in Media
recommendedBooks: Environmental Communication and the Public Sphere - Robert Cox & Phaedra C. Pezzullo, SAGE

units.title: Ecology & Environmental Crises
topics: Climate change, global warming, carbon emissions, deforestation, river pollution (Ganga conservation initiatives)
Biodiversity loss, wildlife conservation laws and sustainable development goals (SDGs)

units.title: Environmental Journalism in Action
topics: Coverage of climate issues, industrial pollution, disaster reporting, environmental activism and eco-campaigns

papers.name: Radio Journalism & Audio Production
recommendedBooks: Radio Production - Robert McLeish, Focal Press
Broadcast Journalism - Andrew Boyd, Focal Press
Other Voices: The Struggle for Community Radio in India - Vinod Pavarala & Kanchan K. Malik, SAGE

units.title: Radio as a Mass Medium
topics: Characteristics, strengths and limitations of radio as an audio medium; History of broadcasting in India: AIR (All India Radio)
FM revolution, private commercial FM channels, Community Radio Stations (CRS) and government licensing guidelines
Internet radio, podcasting revolution and streaming audio platforms (Spotify, Apple Podcasts)

units.title: Radio Formats & Scriptwriting
topics: Radio programming formats: Radio news bulletins, documentaries, radio features, talk shows, phone-in programs, radio drama and radio jingles
Writing for the ear: Conversational style, simplicity, brevity, tone, signposting and phonetic writing
Sound elements: Voice, music (stingers, sting, bed), ambient sound and sound effects (SFX)

units.title: Voice Culture, Anchoring & Interviewing
topics: Microphone types: Dynamic, condenser, omni-directional, bi-directional, cardioid, lavalier and shotgun microphones
Voice culture: Pitch, pace, tone, modulation, pronunciation, breathing techniques and overcoming mic fright
Radio news anchoring and conducting live interviews in studio and over phone

units.title: Digital Audio Recording & Editing Lab
topics: Studio acoustics and digital audio workstations (DAW): Audacity / Adobe Audition tools
Multi-track audio recording, editing, voice leveling, noise reduction, equalization and audio mixing
Practical production of a 5-minute radio news capsule or podcast episode

papers.name: Television Journalism & Video Production
recommendedBooks: Television Production Handbook - Herbert Zettl, Wadsworth
Television Journalism - Ivor Yorke, Focal Press
Broadcast News Handbook - C.A. Tuggle et al., McGraw Hill

units.title: Television Medium & Newsroom Setup
topics: Evolution of television broadcasting in India: Doordarshan, SITE experiment, 1991 Gulf War impact and private satellite 24x7 news channels
Organization of a TV news channel: Input desk, output desk, assignment desk, production control room (PCR) and master control room (MCR)
Roles: Executive Producer, News Anchor, Correspondent, Video Journalist (VJ) and Video Editor

units.title: TV News Gathering & Scripting
topics: Visual grammar: Writing to visuals, split-page script format (Audio vs Video column)
Anatomy of a TV news package: Anchor intro, sound bites (SOT - Sound on Tape), B-roll (cutaways), voice-over (VO) and Piece to Camera (PTC)
Live reporting, running breaking news, breaking news ticker/super and OB van / live mobile backpack (LiveU) setups

units.title: Camera Handling, Lighting & Composition

Camera shots: Extreme long shot (ELS), long shot (LS), medium shot (MS), close-up (CU), extreme close-up (ECU); Camera angles (low, eye, high, Dutch angle)
Camera movements: Pan, tilt, zoom, dolly, tracking; Rule of thirds and 180-degree rule in video composition
Lighting fundamentals: Three-point lighting setup (Key light, Fill light, Back light) and outdoor natural lighting

units.title: Non-Linear Video Editing (NLE) Lab
topics: Principles of video editing: Cut, dissolve, fade, wipe; Continuity editing, jump cut avoidance and montage
Working with editing software: Adobe Premiere Pro / DaVinci Resolve timeline, video-audio synch, transitions and color grading
Practical production of a 2-minute television news package with PTC and sound bites

papers.name: Photojournalism & Visual Storytelling

Basic Critical Theory for Photographers - Ashley la Grange, Focal Press

units.title: Camera Mechanics & Exposure Triangle
topics: History of photography and photojournalism; Camera types: DSLR, Mirrorless, Medium format
The Exposure Triangle: Aperture (f-stop and depth of field), Shutter Speed (motion blur vs freeze action) and ISO (grain/noise)
Lenses: Prime, zoom, wide-angle, telephoto and macro lenses

units.title: Composition & Photojournalistic Ethics
topics: Visual composition rules: Rule of thirds, leading lines, framing, symmetry, patterns and negative space
Photojournalistic storytelling: Hard news photographs, spot news, feature photos, portraits and photo essays
Ethics in photojournalism: Digital manipulation, staged photos, privacy invasion, gruesome imagery and copyright protection

papers.name: Indian Society & Political Economy

India Since Independence - Bipan Chandra, Penguin

units.title: Social Stratification & Contemporary Issues
topics: Caste system, class, religion, linguistic diversity, gender disparities and marginalized communities in India
Agrarian issues, farmer movements, urban migration, poverty and literacy challenges

units.title: Democratic Institutions & Electoral Politics
topics: Indian Parliamentary democracy, Federalism, Center-State relations, Election Commission of India and voting trends
Role of media in shaping public opinion and election coverage

papers.name: Digital Photography & Image Editing Skills
recommendedBooks: Adobe Photoshop Classroom in a Book - Adobe Press

units.title: Hands-on Photography & Darkroom Software
topics: Field photography assignments across Patna: Monuments, riverfront, markets, campus life and portraiture
Adobe Photoshop / Lightroom image post-processing: Cropping, color correction, levels, curves, sharpening and metadata tagging
Curating and presenting a personal photographic portfolio of 10 high-resolution thematic photographs

topics: Definition, role, functions and socio-economic effects of advertising; Advertising vs Sales Promotion vs PR
Types of advertising: Consumer, industrial, trade, retail, financial, institutional and public service advertising (PSA)
AIDA model (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) and DAGMAR approach (Defining Advertising Goals for Measured Advertising Results)

units.title: Advertising Agency Operations
topics: Structure and working of an advertising agency: Account planning, creative department, media planning and client servicing
Agency selection criteria, agency compensation methods (commission system vs fee system)
Self-regulation in advertising: Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) code of ethics

units.title: Creativity, Copywriting & Design
topics: Creative brief preparation; The creative pitch and brainstorming techniques
Copywriting for print: Headline types, subhead, body copy, slogan/tagline, logo and call-to-action (CTA)
Writing commercial scripts for TV commercials (TVC) and radio jingles; Storyboard creation

units.title: Media Planning & Campaign Strategy
topics: Media planning process: Reach, frequency, gross rating points (GRP), cost per thousand (CPM)
Comparative evaluation of print, television, radio, outdoor (OOH) and digital display/social advertising
Designing a complete multi-media advertising campaign for a new brand launch

papers.name: Public Relations & Corporate Communication
recommendedBooks: Effective Public Relations - Cutlip, Center & Broom, Pearson
Corporate Communication - Paul A. Argenti, McGraw Hill
Public Relations in India - J.M. Kaul, Naya Prokash

units.title: Foundations of Public Relations
topics: Meaning, definition, history and evolution of PR in India and internationally; Ivy Lee and Edward Bernays contributions
PR vs Advertising, Publicity, Propaganda and Lobbying; Key publics of PR: Internal vs external publics
Public Relations Society of India (PRSI) and code of professional conduct

units.title: Tools & Media Relations in PR
topics: Media relations: Organizing press conferences, press briefings, press tours and writing effective press releases
Internal communication tools: House journals, newsletters, intranet, bulletin boards, annual reports and town-halls
Corporate publications: Brochures, leaflets, backgrounders and media kits

units.title: Corporate Communication & Crisis PR
topics: Corporate Identity: Corporate vision, brand identity, logo, stationery and organizational reputation management
Crisis Communication: Types of corporate crises, developing a crisis management plan, appointing designated spokesperson and damage control strategies
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR): Planning and communicating social initiatives

units.title: PR Campaign Planning & Evaluation
topics: Steps in planning a PR campaign: Research, action planning, communication execution and post-campaign evaluation
Public opinion polling, media monitoring and press clipping services

papers.name: Development Communication
recommendedBooks: Communication for Development in the Third World - Srinivas R. Melkote & H. Leslie Steeves, SAGE
Development Communication - Uma Narula, Har-Anand Publications

units.title: Concepts & Paradigms of Development
topics: Concept, meaning, indicators and dimensions of development; Human Development Index (HDI)
Dominant paradigm of development (Everett Rogers, Daniel Lerner) and its critique; Participatory development communication model

units.title: Media in Nation Building & Rural Reporting
topics: Role of radio, television and print media in agricultural extension, health, family welfare, education and poverty alleviation
SITE (Satellite Instructional Television Experiment) and Kheda communication projects in India
Designing Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials and community radio campaigns

papers.name: Cinema Studies & Film Appreciation
recommendedBooks: Film Art: An Introduction - David Bordwell & Kristin Thompson, McGraw Hill
Our Films, Their Films - Satyajit Ray, Orient Blackswan

units.title: Film Language & Indian Cinema
topics: Elements of cinema: Mise-en-scene, cinematography, lighting, sound design, editing cuts and montage
Evolution of Indian cinema: Silent era (Raja Harishchandra), studio era, Golden Age of Indian cinema, Parallel/New Wave cinema (Satyajit Ray, Ritwik Ghatak, Mrinal Sen, Shyam Benegal)

units.title: Film Review & Analysis
topics: Film genres: Realism, melodrama, thriller, documentary; Regional cinema of Bihar (Bhojpuri, Maithili cinema history)
Writing critical film reviews: Thematic analysis, directorial vision, performances and technical craft

papers.name: Audio-Video Editing & Podcasting Skills
recommendedBooks: Digital Video Editing: Fundamentals with Premiere Pro - Adobe Press

units.title: Studio Editing Workstation
topics: Timeline workflow, cutting sound bites, audio sweetening and mixing background music in Audacity
Adobe Premiere Pro / Final Cut Pro: Trimming clips, lower-thirds titling, color grading, multi-camera editing
Exporting video in broadcast and web streaming formats (H.264, MP4, 1080p, 4K)

papers.name: New Media & Digital Journalism

Online Journalism: A Basic Text - Tapas Ray, Cambridge University Press
Mobile Journalism: How to Produce News with Your Smartphone - Robb Montgomery, Routledge

Unique characteristics of web journalism: Interactivity, hyper-textuality, multimodality, immediacy, archiving and non-linear consumption
Traditional journalism vs Online journalism: Speed vs accuracy dilemma and the 24x7 news cycle

units.title: Writing for the Web & Search Engine Optimization (SEO)

SEO fundamentals: Keyword research, meta tags, SEO headlines, link building and analytics (Google Analytics overview)
Content Management Systems (CMS): WordPress workspace, publishing posts, uploading media and managing tags

Citizen journalism: Blogging, vlogging, live streaming and community engagement

Data Journalism: Finding public datasets, cleaning data in spreadsheets, basic data visualization charts and storytelling

Newspaper Management - Frank Thayer, Prentice Hall

units.title: Media Economics & Ownership Patterns

units.title: Revenue Models & Newspaper Operations

Production management: Newsprint procurement, printing technology economics, wastage control and space management

Survey research: Questionnaire design, sampling techniques (probability vs non-probability), interviews and focus groups
Audience measurement metrics: TRP (Target Rating Points), TAM, BARC in television, IRS (Indian Readership Survey) in print

Reporting on the Environment - S.L. Becker, McGraw Hill

units.title: Popularizing Science & Health Reporting
topics: Role of media in fostering scientific temper in society; Communicating complex scientific research in accessible lay language
Health and medical journalism: Reporting epidemics, vaccines, public health policy, nutrition and debunking medical myths

units.title: Disasters & Climate Crisis Reporting
topics: Reporting natural disasters: Floods in Bihar, earthquakes, heatwaves and cyclones; Safety guidelines for disaster journalists
Covering industrial pollution, waste management and government environmental initiatives

papers.name: Global Communication & Media Theories

Global Communication - Cees J. Hamelink, SAGE

Agenda Setting Theory (McCombs & Shaw); Framing and Priming in media narratives
Cultivation Theory (George Gerbner) and Mean World Syndrome
Uses and Gratifications Theory: How audiences actively use media to satisfy needs

topics: Frankfurt School: Critical theory, culture industry, commodification and hegemony (Antonio Gramsci)
Information imbalance between Global North and Global South; Flow of news and global news agencies (Reuters, AP, AFP)
New World Information and Communication Order (NWICO) and UNESCO MacBride Commission Report (Many Voices, One World)
Information Society, network society and digital globalization

Sensationalism, yellow journalism, fake news, paid news and private treaties in media
Trial by media, sting operations ethics, privacy intrusion and reporting on juveniles and victims of sexual violence

Introduction to Documentary - Bill Nichols, Indiana University Press

Modes of documentary representation: Expository, observational, participatory, reflexive, poetic and performative modes
Documentary research, proposal writing and shooting treatment script

Post-production: Rough cut, narration voice-over, music score, fine cut, titling and festival distribution
